To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we study the Bi-bilayers/3D top. insulator heterojunction formed under short annealing of the Bi2Te2,4Se0.5 topological insulator.
we have discovered a new type of quantum tunneling heterostructures formed by annealing of the topological materials.
we have observed spin-split Bi-billayer bands interacting with topological insulator-derived bands in the quantum tunneling regime of the Bi-billayer/topological insulator interface.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the electronic structure of a Bi-bilayer grown on top of a Bi2Te2Se topological insulator.
the electronic structure of Bi-bilayer grown on the top of the annealed Bi2Se3.
the electronic structure and spin polarization of Bi-bilayer on 3D topological Bi2Te2Se.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the spin-resolved band structure and the electronic structure of Bi-bilayer on top of the Bi2Te2Se topological insulator have been studied in the quantum dimension tunneling regime.
the spin-polarization of the topological surface states of the 3D TIs is preserved even after the formation of the heterostructure with the 2D TI.

the Bi-bilayers on the top of 3D topological material Bi2Te2Se in the quantum dimension (tunneling) regime can be easily prepared by annealing and the resulting electronic and spin structure can be studied by means of ARPES.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have demonstrated the possibility of forming the spin-resolved Bi-bilayer band structure in the heterostructure Bi-bilayer/Bi2Te2.3Se0.6 in the quantum tunneling regime, which opens a new way for the future low-energy electronics and spin transport devices.
the Bi-bilayers/3D top. insulator in quantum dimension regime is a promising material for future nanoelectronics and spintronic device.
, the annealing-induced Bi-bilayer on Bi2Te2Se is an ideal system to explore the interplay between topological surface states and 2D electron gases.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the quantum spin-Hall effect can be observed not only in the 2D topological insulators, but in the heterostructures with 2D and 3D topological materials as well.
the Bi-bilayers can be used to tune the topological properties of the 3D topological surface states.
the quantum tunneling of Bi-bilayer on the surface of 3D topological materials is an effective way to create the heterojunctions with the spin-polarization of the charge carriers.
